record.paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: Find pairs of quantum channels M and N that are mutually degradable, meaning that there exist channels X and Y for which X ∘ M equals the complementary channel N^C and Y ∘ N equals the complementary channel M^C; in particular, find nontrivial examples beyond the known case M = I, such as pairs where both channels have Choi rank d but are not individually degradable.

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Find pairs of channels M, N that are mutually degradable in the sense that there exist channels X, Y such that X ◦ M = NC Y ◦ N = MC.
At present, the only examples known have M = I which is universal in the sense that N is arbitrary.
It would be particularly interesting to find pairs in which both have Choi-rank d, but are not individually degradable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A, \mathcal{H}_B, \mathcal{H}_C$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear map between spaces of bounded operators on such Hilbert spaces. Every channel $\Phi : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ admits a Stinespring isometry $V : \mathcal{H}_A \to \mathcal{H}_B \otimes \mathcal{H}_E$ with $\Phi(\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}_E(V\rho V^\ast)$; the complementary channel is $\Phi^C(\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}_B(V\rho V^\ast)$, and the Choi rank of $\Phi$ is the minimal such $\dim \mathcal{H}_E$. A channel $\Phi$ is degradable if there exists a channel $D$ with $D \circ \Phi = \Phi^C$.

Call an ordered pair of channels $(M, N)$, with $M : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ and $N : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$, mutually degradable if there exist channels $X$ and $Y$ such that
$$ X \circ M = N^C \quad\text{and}\quad Y \circ N = M^C. $$

Exhibit nontrivial examples of mutually degradable pairs $(M, N)$ beyond the trivial family in which $M$ is the identity channel (in which case $N$ may be arbitrary). In particular, find such pairs in which both $M$ and $N$ have Choi rank equal to $d = \dim \mathcal{H}_A$ and neither $M$ nor $N$ is individually degradable.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for "mutually degradable" quantum channel pairs returns general literature on degradable channels, complementary channels, and Choi rank, but no source explicitly resolving the existence of nontrivial mutually degradable pairs (with both channels of Choi rank $d$ and neither individually degradable). No clear progress on this specific question was located, so the status is taken to be unknown.

status_evidence.title: The structure of degradable quantum channels
status_evidence.snippet: Structural results on degradable channels and Choi rank bounds, but no treatment of mutually degradable pairs.
status_evidence.claim: Standard structural references on degradable channels do not address the mutual degradability problem.

status_evidence.title: Degradable Quantum Channels — Li Yu (CMU notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of degradable channels and qubit cases; no mention of mutually degradable pairs.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of degradable channels do not record progress on mutually degradable pairs.
